# Australian bat lyssavirus infection

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Zoonoses and vector-borne diseases > Australian bat lyssavirus infection*

[Original Article Link](/library/PG0Wzh)

---

## Summary

<u>Australian bat lyssavirus</u> infection is an extremely rare <u>rabies</u>-like condition that is <u>endemic</u> to Australia. It is caused by infection with the <u>Australian bat lyssavirus</u> (<u>ABLV</u>) that is transmitted via infected bats (e.g., bites, scratches). After an <u>incubation period</u> of 3–8 weeks, <u>ABLV</u> infection manifests with <u>flu-like symptoms</u> (e.g., <u>headache</u>, <u>fever</u>, fatigue), followed 1–2 weeks later by severe symptoms, including altered state of consciousness, <u>convulsions</u>, <u>paralysis</u>, and <u>hydrophobia</u>.Diagnosis is confirmed through <u>PCR</u>. Like <u>rabies</u>, <u>ABLV</u> infection is fatal once it breaks out. All <u>animal bites</u> and scratches should be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected. If exposure to <u>ABLV</u> is suspected (i.e., wounds from bats), <u>postexposure prophylaxis</u> using human <u>rabies immunoglobulin</u> and/or <u>rabies vaccine</u> should be initiated immediately.
